questions.q: Ramazan is the month in which the Quran began to be revealed. How, according to the editorial, is this blessing marked?
options: By exchanging costly gifts
Not quite. The article says: By fasting – an act of thanksgiving and acknowledgement – and by reading the Quran with understanding.
By feasting through the day
Not quite. The article says: By fasting – an act of thanksgiving and acknowledgement – and by reading the Quran with understanding.
By fasting – an act of thanksgiving and acknowledgement – and by reading the Quran with understanding
Yes. “O Lord I have heard and I accept.”
By public processions
Not quite. The article says: By fasting – an act of thanksgiving and acknowledgement – and by reading the Quran with understanding.
questions.rationale: “The Quran is a reward from God to His servants. And fasting is acknowledgement of the reward.”

questions.q: How does fasting prepare a person for the study of the Quran?
options: It leaves more hours free in the day
Not quite. The article says: It reduces distractions and dependence on material things, turning attention inward.
It improves the memory through hunger
Not quite. The article says: It reduces distractions and dependence on material things, turning attention inward.
It reduces distractions and dependence on material things, turning attention inward
Right. A prepared mind understands in greater depth.
It keeps one awake at night
Not quite. The article says: It reduces distractions and dependence on material things, turning attention inward.
questions.rationale: “The practice of fasting is also largely aimed at saving a person from distractions… Hence fasting prepares one for the study of the Quran.”

questions.q: The Quran says, “Say your prayers regularly,” but does not set out how. What does this example show about the Hadith?
options: The Hadith supplies the details and the Prophet’s practical example – it is like a commentary on the Quran
Well read. Text and commentary; theory and practice.
The Hadith deals with other subjects
Not quite. The article says: The Hadith supplies the details and the Prophet’s practical example – it is like a commentary on the Quran.
The Hadith replaces the Quran
Not quite. The article says: The Hadith supplies the details and the Prophet’s practical example – it is like a commentary on the Quran.
The Hadith is part of the Quran
Not quite. The article says: The Hadith supplies the details and the Prophet’s practical example – it is like a commentary on the Quran.
questions.rationale: “It is as if the Quran is the text and the Hadith its commentary; the Quran being theory and Hadith being the practice.”

questions.q: Which of these does the article list among the tasks of the angels?
options: Deciding who will be rewarded
Not quite. The article says: Carrying out God’s commands in the universe and keeping a record of human actions.
Carrying out God’s commands in the universe and keeping a record of human actions
Yes. They also brought God’s word to the prophets.
Creating new forms of life
Not quite. The article says: Carrying out God’s commands in the universe and keeping a record of human actions.
Changing the laws of nature at will
Not quite. The article says: Carrying out God’s commands in the universe and keeping a record of human actions.
questions.rationale: “It is they who carry out His commandments and communicate His word to the prophets. They preserve a record of man’s actions.”

questions.q: After Moses watered the flocks at Midian, one of the daughters urged her father to hire him. What reason did she give?
options: “He comes from a noble family”
Not quite. The article says: “The best man to hire is someone strong and trustworthy”.
“He is a stranger and needs shelter”
Not quite. The article says: “The best man to hire is someone strong and trustworthy”.
“He asked for very little”
Not quite. The article says: “The best man to hire is someone strong and trustworthy”.
“The best man to hire is someone strong and trustworthy”
Correct. Hard work and honesty – a two-point formula for success.
questions.rationale: “One of the girls said, ‘Father, hire him! for the best man to hire is someone strong and trustworthy.’ (28: 26)”

questions.q: Why, according to the article, does the Quran aim first at the individual’s thinking rather than at the system?
options: Because individuals are easier to command
Not quite. The article says: Because the system depends on individuals, not the other way round.
Because society is unimportant
Not quite. The article says: Because the system depends on individuals, not the other way round.
Because the system depends on individuals, not the other way round
Right. Change the person and the rest follows.
Because systems cannot be changed
Not quite. The article says: Because the system depends on individuals, not the other way round.
questions.rationale: “The actual target of the Book is to change the thinking of the individual… This is because the system is subservient to the individual and not vice versa.”

questions.q: In social life, what decides whether we meet friendship or hostility from another person?
options: Whether we speak the same language
Not quite. The article says: Whether we have stirred his conscience or his ego.
Whether we met him by day or night
Not quite. The article says: Whether we have stirred his conscience or his ego.
Whether we are richer than he is
Not quite. The article says: Whether we have stirred his conscience or his ego.
Whether we have stirred his conscience or his ego
Well reasoned. Touch the ego and expect reaction.
questions.rationale: “If the ego is touched, we will face reaction from the other side. However, if we awaken a person’s conscience we will see antagonism turn to friendship.”

questions.q: What does the article mean by jihad bin nafs?
options: A debate with opponents
Not quite. The article says: The inner struggle to control negative feelings such as arrogance, jealousy, greed and anger.
A journey to distant lands
Not quite. The article says: The inner struggle to control negative feelings such as arrogance, jealousy, greed and anger.
A period of fasting
Not quite. The article says: The inner struggle to control negative feelings such as arrogance, jealousy, greed and anger.
The inner struggle to control negative feelings such as arrogance, jealousy, greed and anger
Yes. A lifelong effort to stay on the right path.
questions.rationale: “Jihad is of two kinds. One is with the self (jihad bin nafs), that is making the maximum effort to keep control over negative feelings.”

questions.q: What did the Prophet pray on sighting the new moon of Ramazan?
options: That the month might come “with peace and security”
Exactly. Ramazan is the month of patience and self-control.
That the month might bring wealth
Not quite. The article says: That the month might come “with peace and security”.
That the month might bring victory over others
Not quite. The article says: That the month might come “with peace and security”.
That the month might pass quickly
Not quite. The article says: That the month might come “with peace and security”.
questions.rationale: “O God, let the moon of the month of Ramazan appear on us with peace and security.”

questions.q: Which description fits those whom the article calls deserving of Paradise?
options: People who restrain their ego, credit God for their achievements, and gladly take the back seat
Well read. Living “with the blameless innocence of flowers.”
People who never met any difficulty
Not quite. The article says: People who restrain their ego, credit God for their achievements, and gladly take the back seat.
People who are known to everyone
Not quite. The article says: People who restrain their ego, credit God for their achievements, and gladly take the back seat.
People who always sit in the front row
Not quite. The article says: People who restrain their ego, credit God for their achievements, and gladly take the back seat.
questions.rationale: “These are the worthy individuals who relish taking the back seats while others scramble for the front rows.”
